syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Meaning of accounting and the accounting process

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of accounting as defined by AICPA and AAA.
Distinguish external and internal economic events and identify the transactions an event comprises.
Explain identification, measurement, recording and communication as steps of the accounting process.

topics.title: Users of accounting information and their needs

concepts.learning_objective: Classify users of accounting information as internal or external users.
Identify the information each user group seeks from accounting reports.

topics.title: Accounting as a source of information and its branches

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why accounting is a source of information and a means of disseminating it to users.
Distinguish financial accounting, cost accounting and management accounting.

topics.title: Qualitative characteristics of accounting information

concepts.learning_objective: Explain reliability and relevance as qualities that make accounting information decision-useful.
Explain understandability and comparability and recognise when they are violated.

topics.title: Objectives and role of accounting

concepts.learning_objective: State the objectives of accounting, including ascertaining profit or loss and financial position.
Describe the different roles of accounting such as language of business and historical record.
Recognise that accounting information is historical, quantitative and financial in nature.

topics.title: Basic terms: entity, transaction, assets, liabilities and capital

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the business entity and decide whether an event is a transaction of that entity.
Classify assets and liabilities as current or non-current.
Explain capital and its treatment as a claim of the owner on the business.

topics.title: Basic terms: revenue, expenses, expenditure, profit, gain and loss

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish revenue, expense, revenue expenditure and capital expenditure.
Compute profit and distinguish it from gain and loss.

topics.title: Basic terms: discount, voucher, goods, drawings, purchases, stock, debtors and creditors

concepts.learning_objective: Explain trade discount, cash discount and vouchers.
Decide when an item is goods for a business and identify drawings by the owner.
Explain stock, debtors and creditors and their place in the balance sheet.

topics.title: Need for a theory base and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why accounting needs a theory base to make information reliable and comparable.
Describe the meaning, evolution and changing nature of GAAP.

topics.title: Business entity, money measurement and going concern

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the business entity concept to capital, drawings and personal transactions of the owner.
Identify what can be recorded under money measurement and state its limitation.
Explain how the going concern assumption allows the cost of an asset to be spread over its life.

topics.title: Accounting period, cost and dual aspect

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of accounting period and the periods for which statements are prepared.
Calculate the cost at which an asset is recorded and evaluate the historical cost basis.
Analyse the two-fold effect of transactions using the accounting equation.

topics.title: Revenue recognition, matching and full disclosure

concepts.learning_objective: Determine when revenue is realised, including time-based incomes.
Apply the matching concept to expenses and the cost of goods sold.
State what the full disclosure concept requires of financial statements.

topics.title: Consistency, conservatism, materiality and objectivity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why consistent accounting policies are needed for comparison.
Apply the prudence rule of providing for all losses but not anticipating profits.
Distinguish material from immaterial items and explain the need for verifiable evidence.

topics.title: Systems and basis of accounting

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the double entry system from the single entry system.
Compare the cash basis and the accrual basis of accounting and compute profit under each.

topics.title: Accounting standards

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning, issuing body and objectives of accounting standards.
Evaluate the benefits and limitations of accounting standards.

topics.title: Goods and Services Tax
topics.ncert_sections: Goods and Services Tax (One Country One Tax)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain GST as a destination-based tax and state its features and advantages.
Apply CGST, SGST and IGST to intra-state and inter-state supplies.

topics.title: Business Transactions and Source Documents

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a business transaction is an exchange of economic consideration with a give and a take aspect recorded in at least two accounts.
Identify source documents such as cash memo, invoice, pay-in-slip and cheque as evidence on which all recording is based.

topics.title: Preparation of Accounting Vouchers

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish transaction, debit, credit and journal (complex) vouchers by the number of debits and credits involved.
State the essential elements an accounting voucher must contain and how long vouchers are preserved.

topics.title: Accounting Equation

concepts.learning_objective: State the accounting equation A = L + C and use its derived forms to find a missing figure.
Analyse the effect of transactions on assets, liabilities and capital and show that the equation stays balanced.

topics.title: Using Debit and Credit

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the T-account and explain that debit means the left side and credit the right side of an account.
Apply the rules of debit and credit to assets, liabilities, capital, expenses and revenues.

topics.title: Books of Original Entry and the Journal

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the journal as the book of original entry and the purpose of its columns, narration and L.F.
Record simple and compound journal entries for transactions involving two or more accounts.
Record journal entries for purchases and sales under CGST, SGST and IGST and compute net GST payable after set-off.

topics.title: The Ledger and Posting from Journal

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the ledger as the principal book and distinguish it from the journal.
Classify ledger accounts into permanent accounts and temporary accounts.
Describe the steps of posting journal entries to the debit and credit sides of ledger accounts.

topics.title: Special purpose books and the single column cash book

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the journal is sub-divided into special purpose books and what the journal proper records.
Record cash transactions in a single column cash book and post them to the ledger.

topics.title: Double column cash book

concepts.learning_objective: Record and identify contra entries between the cash and bank columns of a cash book.
Record cheques received, deposits, bank charges, overdraft and dishonoured cheques in the bank column.

topics.title: Petty cash book

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the imprest system of maintaining petty cash and calculate the amount reimbursed.
Prepare an analytical petty cash book and post its column totals to the ledger.

topics.title: Balancing of cash book

concepts.learning_objective: Balance a cash book and explain why its cash column cannot show a credit balance.
Identify the source documents (vouchers) used for recording entries in the cash book.

topics.title: Purchases book and purchases return book

concepts.learning_objective: Record credit purchases of goods at net invoice value in the purchases book and post them.
Record returns to suppliers in the purchases return book on the basis of debit notes.

topics.title: Sales book and sales return book

concepts.learning_objective: Record credit sales of goods in the sales book and post them to customers' accounts and sales account.
Record returns from customers in the sales return book on the basis of credit notes.

topics.title: Journal proper

concepts.learning_objective: Identify opening, adjustment, rectification and transfer entries recorded in the journal proper.
Identify other transactions, such as credit purchase of assets and goods withdrawn, that go to the journal proper.

topics.title: Balancing the accounts

concepts.learning_objective: Balance a ledger account using balance c/d and balance b/d and state the nature of its balance.
Explain that expense, loss and revenue accounts are closed by transfer instead of being carried forward.

topics.title: Meaning of passbook and need for reconciliation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what a bank passbook records and how its balance relates to the bank column of the cash book.
State the meaning of a bank reconciliation statement and why a firm prepares it.

topics.title: Timing differences

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how cheques issued but not presented and cheques deposited but not collected cause a difference between the two balances.
Identify direct debits, direct deposits, collections and standing-instruction payments made by the bank and their effect on the passbook balance.
Explain the effect of a dishonoured cheque or discounted bill on the passbook balance.

topics.title: Differences caused by errors

concepts.learning_objective: Identify errors made by the firm in the cash book and work out their effect on the reconciliation.
Identify errors made by the bank in the passbook and work out their effect on the reconciliation.

topics.title: Preparing the statement with favourable balances

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of a favourable balance as per the cash book and as per the passbook.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement starting from a favourable balance as per the cash book.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement starting from a favourable balance as per the passbook.

topics.title: Dealing with overdrafts

concepts.learning_objective: State what an overdraft is and how it appears in the cash book and the passbook.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement when the cash book or the passbook shows an overdraft.

chapters.title: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors

topics.title: Meaning and objectives of a trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of a trial balance and the purpose it serves in the accounting process.
Explain why a tallied trial balance checks arithmetical accuracy but is not conclusive proof of correct accounts.
Identify whether an account normally shows a debit or a credit balance in the trial balance.

topics.title: Methods of preparing a trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: Prepare a trial balance by showing the debit and credit totals of each ledger account.
Prepare a trial balance from ledger balances and explain why this method is most used.
Describe the four-column totals-cum-balances method and its limitations.

topics.title: Significance of agreement and classification of errors

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish errors of commission from errors of complete and partial omission.
Identify errors of principle arising from wrong capital-revenue classification.
Explain how compensating errors leave the trial balance in agreement.

topics.title: Searching of errors

concepts.learning_objective: List the steps an accountant takes to detect errors when the trial balance does not tally.
Use half of the difference to trace an amount posted to the wrong side.
Recognise that a difference divisible by 9 suggests a transposition of figures.

topics.title: Rectification of errors not affecting the trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why two-sided errors do not affect the trial balance and are corrected by a journal entry.
Pass the rectifying journal entry for errors of omission, commission and principle in two accounts.

topics.title: Suspense account and errors affecting the trial balance

concepts.learning_objective: Rectify one-sided errors such as wrong posting and wrong casting through a suspense account.
Explain when a suspense account is opened, on which side it appears and how it is closed.
State the account used when errors of one year are rectified in the next accounting year.

topics.title: Meaning of depreciation, depletion and amortisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain depreciation as the expired cost of a fixed asset allocated over its useful life, and state its features.
Distinguish depreciation from depletion of natural resources and amortisation of intangible assets.

topics.title: Causes of and need for depreciation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify wear and tear, expiry of legal rights, obsolescence and abnormal factors as causes of depreciation.
Explain why depreciation is charged: matching, tax, true and fair position and compliance with law.

topics.title: Factors affecting the amount of depreciation

concepts.learning_objective: Determine the cost of a fixed asset including all expenses to put it in working condition.
Calculate net residual value and depreciable cost of an asset.
Explain the estimated useful life of an asset and how it differs from physical life.

topics.title: Straight line and written down value methods

concepts.learning_objective: Compute annual depreciation and its rate under the straight line method.
Compute depreciation and book value under the written down value method.
Compare the straight line and written down value methods on basis, charge, tax recognition and suitability.

topics.title: Recording depreciation, disposal and additions to assets

concepts.learning_objective: Record depreciation by charging it to the asset account or through a provision for depreciation account.
Record the sale of an asset and compute the profit or loss on its disposal.
Apply AS-6 (Revised) to depreciation on additions and extensions to an existing asset.

topics.title: Provisions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain provisions as charges against profit for known liabilities or losses of uncertain amount.
Calculate and record a provision for doubtful debts after writing off bad debts.

topics.title: Reserves and secret reserve

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a reserve, an appropriation of profit, from a provision, a charge against profit.
Classify reserves as general or specific and as revenue or capital reserves.
Explain how a secret reserve is created and its effect on disclosed profits.
